terms.meaning: The body of world nations set up on 24 October 1945 for lasting peace; first called UNO.
The continents with olive branches on two sides, standing for peace and friendship.
The power of any one permanent member to block a Security Council decision.

items.name: Why the UN was formed
items.formula: World War II (1939-45) killed about four crore people.
items.example: 51 nations met at San Francisco, led by Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin.

items.name: Aims of the UN
items.formula: Keep world peace and security, build friendly relations, solve economic and social problems together, respect human rights.

items.name: General Assembly
items.formula: The UN's "Parliament": meets every September; each member has 5 representatives but one vote.

items.name: Security Council
items.formula: 15 members: 5 permanent (USA, Russia, Britain, France, China) and 10 elected for two years.
items.example: A resolution needs nine votes and no permanent member's veto.

items.name: Economic and Social Council
items.formula: Works on human rights, illiteracy, poverty, hunger, refugees, health and equality for women.
items.example: It also covers child protection and drug control.

items.name: International Court of Justice
items.formula: At The Hague in the Netherlands, with 15 judges elected by the General Assembly and Security Council.
items.example: It settles disputes between member nations.

items.name: Secretariat and Secretary-General
items.formula: The Secretary-General heads the Secretariat; at present Antonio Guterres (Portugal).
items.example: The General Assembly chooses, with the Security Council's approval.

items.name: Trusteeship Council
items.formula: Formed with 5 members to protect 11 territories that weren't self-governing.

items.name: UN agencies and their head offices
items.formula: UNESCO: Paris. FAO: Rome. WHO: Geneva. UNICEF: New York.
items.example: The UN flag is light blue with the emblem.

items.name: Achievements of the UN
items.formula: Aid to refugees and children, help for new nations, preventing another world war.
items.example: Its limits: no army of its own, and the veto can block decisions.

items.name: India and the UN
items.formula: A signatory of the 1945 Charter; against racism and colonialism; first to call for a nuclear test ban.
items.example: Vijayalakshmi Pandit was the first woman to chair the UN; Nagendra Singh was Chief Justice of the ICJ.

mistakes.text: India is not a permanent member of the Security Council; the five are USA, Russia, Britain, France and China.
The General Assembly is the UN's "Parliament"; the Security Council is like its executive.
Nine votes alone aren't enough: one permanent member's veto still blocks a resolution.
